title: A Certain Scientific Railgun
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: In Academy City, a near-future city of students trained to develop psychic powers, Mikoto Misaka is one of only seven top-ranked 'Level 5' espers. With her friend Kuroko Shirai and the student-run law enforcement group Judgment, she investigates incidents such as the 'Level Upper' affair and uncovers dark secrets about the city's experiments (Wikipedia; Seven Seas blurb via AniList).
life_message: Loyal friends who act on their own sense of justice can stand up to powerful institutions that treat people as experiments.

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Mikoto handles threats personally; Judgment works through rules (Wikipedia; Seven Seas blurb).

Order vs freedom.evidence: Heroine pursues truth beyond official channels, exposing the city's secrets (publisher blurb).

Civic vs kin.evidence: Close circle of friends Kuroko, Uiharu and Saten is the core loyalty (Wikipedia).

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Level 1 to 5 ranking is central; story questions its costs (MU Ranking System; to verify).

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Science city where powers come from curriculum and research (AniList blurb).

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: School-life comedy beside danger (AniList Cute Girls Doing Cute Things).

folkways.japan: Middle-school girls' friendships, a prestigious girls' academy and a student disciplinary committee reflect Japanese school culture and the light-novel franchise tradition.

delivery.evidence: Sources say nothing on delivery (to verify); summaries show themes carried by the investigation plot.
delivery.note: The critique of the city's experiments appears to come through what Mikoto discovers rather than speeches, as far as summaries show.

winners_losers: Mikoto and her friends prevail through loyalty; the city's secret researchers lose sympathy. The worldview favored is personal conscience over institutional science.
